title: The Tenderloin district and Freddie Keppard at the Dreamland
summary: Punch played blues in the district; he did not know Jelly Roll, Tony Jackson or Oliver there but worked with Keppard and Doc Cook in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: The district. Oh hell yeah man. You was. I was playing with a fellow and Ken Beard in the daytime. Cans of the women, you know, the whole hustle of them. 10 cents a can and every night I'd get up there and play the blues with the piano player. Now he, I forget his name, he died. He was a sickly fellow but he died. But I, nothing but blues all night. I'd sit up and play the blues all night. A fellow named Tootlum. Tootlum. Gravity and Gravy. All right let me ask you this. It's known that Jelly Roll played here in the Tenderloins. Well let me tell you this. But there must have, did you ever hear of Tony Jackson? Yeah, whoever. I'm fixing to tell you now. I didn't know Jelly Roll here. You didn't? And I didn't know Tony Jackson here. Them fellow was gone I got here. King Oliver was gone. Johnny Dots was gone. I met them in Chicago. Freddy Keppert was gone. That's right. I worked with Freddy Keppert at the Dream Land. In Chicago? Did you work with Doc Cook? Yes sir. You worked with Doc Cook. That's right. That's right. That's sir.
Which band was it that Keppert was in you were in?
Keppert, he had his honor band then.
And you were with him huh?
